chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever visits a sick person from among the Muslims, Allah appoints with him forever seventy thousand angels who envelop his dwelling, glorifying therein, sanctifying, proclaiming the unity of God, and proclaiming God's greatness until the Day of Resurrection — half of their prayers being for the visitor of the sick.

key_terms.عَادَ: Visited (the sick) — عيادة المريض (visiting the sick) is one of the rights a Muslim has upon another
key_terms.نِصْفُ صَلَاتِهِمْ: Half of their prayers — angelic intercession apportioned to the visitor
key_terms.وَكَّلَ: Assigned/appointed — from tawkil, to entrust with a task or responsibility
key_terms.يَغْشَوْنَ رَحْلَهُ: Envelop his dwelling — a vivid image of angelic protection and presence surrounding the visitor's home
key_terms.يُسَبِّحُونَ / يُقَدِّسُونَ / يُهَلِّلُو: Glorifying / Sanctifying / Proclaiming tawhid / Proclaiming greatness — the four major formulas of divine remembrance

ai.seo_question: What reward does Islam promise for visiting the sick according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that visiting a sick Muslim is an act of profound spiritual merit. The reward described — 70,000 angels permanently assigned to the visitor's home, performing continuous acts of worship until the Day of Judgment — reflects the enormous spiritual weight that early Islamic tradition placed on fulfilling the rights of fellow believers. The concluding clause, that half of these angels' prayers are dedicated to the visitor, emphasizes that this communal act generates ongoing intercession for the visitor.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Safwan Al Jammal, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who visits a sick one from the Muslims, Allahazwj would Allocate with him, forever, seventy thousand from the Angels enveloping his ride, and they would be seeking Forgiveness for him in it, and Extolling and Sanctifying and Exclaiming the Greatness of Allahazwj up to the Day of Judgement, half of their Salaats being for the visitor of the sick one’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Najran from Safwan al- Jammal who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

if one visits a Muslim patient, Allah assigns seventy thousand angels who come to his house saying Tasbih, Taqdis, Tahlil and Takbir up to the Day of Judgment. Half of their Salah (prayer) is for the visitor of the patient.”
